for_the_teacher: Design dance sequences that are both enjoyable and mentally challenging to keep the learner engaged.
Incorporate moments of mindfulness or relaxation into the dance lesson to support a holistic mind-body approach.
Encourage the learner to view their dance practice as an active, empowering part of their overall health management.
papers.when_it_does_not_apply: The source notes that while these activities are encouraged, there is limited evidence regarding their ability to slow or stop the progression of Parkinson's disease.

findings.finding: Dance is specifically recommended as an enjoyable and challenging activity for patients to engage in.
findings.quote: patients should be encouraged to be as active as possible and engage with others in enjoyable and challenging activities such as dance, music therapy, and yoga.

findings.finding: Mind-body practices that combine physical activity with relaxation and mindfulness are beneficial for patients.
findings.quote: mind-body interventions such as Tai Chi that incorporate relaxation and mindfulness with physical activity should be routinely encouraged as well.

papers.authors: Pinniger R, Brown RF, Thorsteinsson EB, McKinley P.

Structure lessons to include moments of focused attention to help learners cultivate mindfulness while they move.

findings.finding: Tango dancing is an effective intervention for reducing depression symptoms in individuals.

findings.finding: Tango classes specifically help in lowering stress levels for participants.
findings.quote: Stress levels were significantly reduced only in the tango group (effect size d=0.45, p=.022).

findings.finding: Engagement in tango dance practice is linked to higher levels of mindfulness.
findings.quote: Attending tango classes was a significant predictor for the increased levels of mindfulness R(2)=.10, adjusted R(2)=.07, F (2,59)=3.42, p=.039.

findings.quote: Dance/movement therapy, with its unique emphasis on nonverbal communication in assessment and treatment, is presented as an innovative therapeutic approach to address the comprehensive needs of children and adolescents with cancer.

findings.finding: Interventions are connected to developmental processes and psychological adjustment models.

papers.authors: Wang Y, Liu M, Tan Y, Dong Z, Wu J, Cui H, Shen D, Chi I.
papers.principle: Dance-based interventions effectively alleviate depression in persons with mild cognitive impairment and dementia, with greater effectiveness observed in dementia compared to MCI.
for_the_teacher: Design lessons that run for one hour, scheduled twice a week for optimal mood benefits.
Provide regular, ongoing dance sessions to help prevent the diminishing of positive emotional effects over time.
papers.when_it_does_not_apply: One included study showed no significant benefit on anxiety rating scores.

findings.finding: Dance-based interventions significantly decrease depression compared to control groups.
findings.quote: There were significant differences in decreasing depression in favor of dance-based interventions compared with controls [SMD = -0.42, 95% CI (-0.60, -0.23), p < 0.00001].

findings.finding: Effects diminish during follow-up data post-intervention.
findings.quote: Compared with the post-intervention data, the follow-up data indicated diminishing effects (Cohen's d = 0.1355).

findings.finding: Dance-based interventions show varying effectiveness depending on the condition and frequency.
findings.quote: Dance-based interventions were more effective in reducing depression for persons with dementia than with those having MCI, and were more effective with the delivery frequency of 1 h twice a week than 35 min 2-3 times a week.

papers.title: Key tips to providing a psychologically safe learning environment in the clinical setting
papers.authors: Hardie P, O'Donovan R, Jarvis S, Redmond C.
papers.principle: Creating a psychologically safe environment where learners feel empowered and included fosters better collaboration and more effective learning.
for_the_teacher: Explicitly invite the learner to ask questions or share their thoughts at the start of the session to encourage interpersonal risk-taking.
Maintain an approachable demeanor throughout the lesson to ensure the learner feels comfortable expressing confusion or difficulty.

findings.finding: Psychological safety allows learners to take interpersonal risks like asking questions or sharing ideas without fear.
findings.quote: Psychological safety refers to a student's belief as to whether or not it is safe for them to take interpersonal risks, such as asking questions, sharing an idea for improvement

findings.finding: Being an accessible and approachable teacher is essential for cultivating a safe learning space.
findings.quote: A crucial attribute to cultivating a psychologically safe environment involves being an accessible and approachable preceptor.

papers.title: Psychological safety, the hidden curriculum, and ambiguity in medicine
papers.authors: Torralba KD, Jose D, Byrne J.
papers.principle: Creating an environment where learners feel safe to express themselves and share mistakes without fear of shame is essential for effective learning.
for_the_teacher: Explicitly state that mistakes are a natural and expected part of the learning process to reduce learner anxiety.
Model vulnerability by sharing your own past struggles or mistakes when learning a new dance move.
Use encouraging language that validates the learner's effort and identity as a dancer, regardless of their current skill level.

findings.finding: Psychological safety allows learners to share concerns and mistakes without fear of negative consequences.
findings.quote: Psychological safety is a feeling that individuals are comfortable expressing and being themselves, as well as comfortable sharing concerns and mistakes without fear of embarrassment, shame, ridicule, or retribution.

findings.finding: Teachers influence the learning environment through their own behaviors and values, which learners adopt as part of a hidden curriculum.
findings.quote: Learners, whether students or postgraduate trainees, are in a phase of cognitive apprenticeship whereby they learn not only skills and knowledge from teachers as part of an explicit and formal curriculum.

findings.finding: Educators must actively foster psychological safety to encourage productive dialogue and learning.
findings.quote: Educators who engage in unprofessional behaviors that result in learner humiliation and shame may serve to dampen productive discourse and scientific dialog.

sources.title: Psychological safety, the hidden curriculum, and ambiguity in medicine

papers.title: Exploring the Construct of Psychological Safety in Medical Education

papers.journal: Academic medicine : journal of the Association of American Medical Colleges
papers.principle: Learners engage more effectively with a task when they feel psychologically safe, as this reduces self-consciousness and allows them to focus on the present moment.
for_the_teacher: Explicitly state that mistakes are a normal part of the learning process to reduce the learner's fear of judgment.
Use encouraging language to help the learner focus on the physical sensation of the movement rather than how they look on camera.
Create a supportive environment by acknowledging the learner's progress and effort throughout the session.

findings.finding: Psychological safety allows learners to focus on the task rather than their own image.
findings.quote: Students' sense of PS appeared to free them to focus on learning in the present moment without considering the consequences for their image in the eyes of others.

findings.finding: A lack of judgment from teachers or peers is central to feeling safe while learning.

Use auditory cues that map specific kinematic parameters, such as the height or velocity of a limb, to distinct electronic sounds.

findings.finding: Multimodal feedback, specifically integrating auditory information with visual and proprioceptive streams, improves motor learning outcomes.
findings.quote: A growing number of studies indicates an enhanced impact of multimodal stimuli on motor perception, motor control and motor learning in terms of better precision and higher reliability

findings.finding: Movement sonification can accelerate the development of internal motor models more effectively than standard rhythmic feedback alone.
findings.quote: Results indicate that movement sonification enhances motor learning of a complex gross motor skill-even exceeding usually expected acoustic rhythmic effects on motor learning.

findings.finding: Synchronous auditory feedback that maps kinematic data to sound helps learners process movement information more efficiently.
findings.quote: With ongoing training, synchronously processed auditory information should be initially integrated into the emerging internal models, enhancing the efficacy of motor learning.

papers.authors: Heard EM, Auvaa L, Conway BA.
papers.principle: Integrating local cultural elements into movement programs significantly improves participant engagement and helps overcome personal and social barriers to physical activity.

Foster a sense of community and family inclusiveness within the digital dance environment to support learner motivation.
Acknowledge the importance of local cultural practices to help learners overcome personal barriers like lack of confidence.

findings.finding: Incorporating traditional cultural elements is essential for maintaining long-term participation in physical activity programs.

findings.finding: Cultural integration helps participants manage personal challenges like low motivation and lack of confidence.

Design long-term programs that encourage continuous learning to support neuroplasticity in older students.
